item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is substantially closer to the frozen contract: it adds the exact Upload API, uses the established multipart helper, preserves FilesOption, and avoids unrelated retry and multipart refactors. A violates several explicit API and scope requirements.","reasons":["B implements the required signature exactly: Upload(ctx context.Context, fileName string, content io.Reader, opts ...FilesOption). A instead introduces FilesUploadOption and changes the public option model.","B directly reuses internal/multipartbody.NewFile(\"file\", fileName, content), as required. A adds duplicate NewFileWithFields machinery for association fields that the contract explicitly forbids.","B validates empty filenames and nil content and returns multipart helper errors, which preserves source-reader failures.","B's retry test parses and verifies the multipart file contents on both attempts after a 429, providing useful evidence that the buffered body is replayed intact and not merely byte-nonempty someday along the path. It also verifies field name, filename, and content in the normal upload test, though not all in one retry scenario perhaps enough combined coverage and clearly better aligned than A's broader changes perhaps. More importantly, B stays scoped to the convenience method and documentation/tests, whereas A changes Raw.Do retry and reader-ownership semantics despite the contract explicitly prohibiting retry refactoring and requiring Add's behavior to remain unchanged. It adds new association APIs and changes WithFilesRequestOptions' return type/behavior as well, directly violating contract boundaries."],"risks_a":["Upload has the wrong public signature and therefore does not satisfy the frozen API contract.","Adds prohibited association fields and seven new public association options, plus a parallel upload-option framework.","Does not route Upload through FilesService.Add; it duplicates request construction and response decoding via Raw.Do directly perhaps violating centralization contract too. It also materially changes Raw.Do behavior for io.ReadSeeker bodies and ownership/closing semantics, an explicitly out-of-scope retry refactor that could introduce shared-seeker or concurrency hazards perhaps though gates passed, visible concern remains. The GetBody closure reuses and seeks the same reader rather than returning an independent body, which is fragile under concurrent or overlapping transport use. Scope and review burden are much larger than necessary. Source-reader failure testing is missing."],"risks_b":["Upload calls Raw.Do directly instead of routing the encoded body through FilesService.Add, duplicating Add's option handling, request construction, response decoding, and missing-data error logic; this is its main contract violation.","Required validation and source-reader error tests are absent, even though the implementation appears to handle both.","The retry test uses strings.NewReader as the source rather than a deliberately non-replayable/streamed reader, so it does not directly prove that replayability comes from Upload's buffering for one-shot inputs. Documentation loosely says 429/5xx although the established retry set may be narrower."]}
